Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

continue verb

also go on, carry on, keep on, keep going, go on with, keep (doing), keep doing, proceed

classical

Plaut. Amph. 803: perge porrō dīcere
Mart. 14.163.1: lūdere pergis?

pergō, pergere, perrēxī, perrēctum

verb, third conjugation

go on, continue

With an infinitive, or alone: Perge!, “go on!”, to someone telling a story; Cicero uses it only with an infinitive (Lewis & Short). “Not stop doing” is nōn dēsinere with an infinitive.

Other words

  • persevērō, persevērāre, persevērāvī, persevērātum — keep on, persist

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 4.1: persevērā ut coepistī

    With an infinitive, or in and the ablative.

  • continuō, continuāre, continuāvī, continuātum — continue without a break

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Caes. BC 3.36: diē ac nocte continuātō itinere (Lewis & Short)

    Transitive: to keep something going without a pause.

Examples

  • Nē interpellā. perge porrō dīcere.

    Don’t interrupt. Go on with the story.Plaut. Amph. 803

  • redde pilam: sonat aes thermārum. lūdere pergis?

    give back the ball: the bell of the baths is ringing. Are you still playing?Mart. 14.163.1

  • persevērā ut coepistī

    keep on as you beganSen. Ep. 4.1

See also stop.
